prompt.text:
Pixel-art sprite sheet for a horizontal arcade shoot-'em-up: the two animation frames of the DARTER enemy — a small arrowhead fighter flying to the LEFT, engine flickering.

Design identity to keep exactly — a flat dart-shaped fighter seen from above, nose pointing LEFT: warm yellow armour body (#e8c040) with darker ochre under-plate (#8a6a18) along the rear edges, a white-hot canopy glint (#fff8c0) just behind the pointed nose, swept-back wing roots tapering to the tail, and a small red engine block (#e84818) glowing at the tail centre, all on a 1-px near-black outline (#101820). The fighter is WIDER than tall (about 1.75:1), sleek and fast-reading, and stays a small compact chip of about 150 px wide by 90 px tall inside its 288×256 cell, deep in flat green with at least 60 px of clear key on every side.

Rebuild it as a sprite sheet under this strict contract:
- On a CONTINUOUS flat pure bright green chroma-key background, exactly hex #51e018, identical solid colour in every background pixel: no gradient, no vignette, no shadow, no floor plane, no panel, no second green shade.
- EXACTLY 2 cells laid out as 1 ROW OF 2 (2-column by 1-row) — every cell holding exactly ONE fighter; a missing, empty or merged cell ruins the entire sheet.
- Cells in reading order (left-right, then top-bottom):
  cell 1 = the fighter with its engine at REST — a short, dim red flame stub at the tail. The subject lies within aspect 1.35:1 to 2.30:1.
  cell 2 = the EXACT fighter of cell 1 redrawn at the identical pixel size and position — then only the tail flame block recoloured to a hotter red-orange core. Same silhouette, same length, same width: the flicker changes flame COLOUR only, adding no pixels to the outline at all. Aspect stays inside 1.35:1 to 2.20:1.
- The sheet canvas measures EXACTLY 576×256 px. Produce EXACTLY 2 subject cells — no more, no fewer — and nothing else on the sheet.
- Each subject sits well inside its cell with at least 12 px of unbroken flat #51e018 around it and clean flat gutters between cells: no subject may touch or cross a cell edge; keep every subject within the inner 75% of its cell.
- CENTRING AND SIZE: every subject sits at the exact centre of its cell at the same scale and position as the other cell — only the named state changes.
- NO guide lines, NO cell borders, NO divider lines, NO frames, NO text, NO labels, NO numbers anywhere on the sheet — the cell names above are ordering instructions and must NEVER be drawn.
- Style: the finest retro pixel art for its native resolution — as much detail and inner structure as possible AT that low resolution, crisp hard-edged square pixels, chunky bold forms, a rich four-to-six step shading ramp lit from the top-left with careful inner detail and real material texture, clean saturated colours, a 1-px near-black outline on every silhouette edge, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no smooth gradients.
prompt.negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text, letters, labels, numbers, cell borders, guide lines, grid lines, watermark, signature, blurry, anti-aliasing, smooth gradient background, scenery, stars, cast shadow, drop shadow, multiple subjects per cell, empty cell, cropped subject, subject touching edge

notes:
enemies/darter (2f 21×12 served; arrowhead fighter flying left, flickering engine) incl its auto-derived @flash sibling — the 2 cells cropped to their measured subject boxes with the 6-px key border clamped inside each cell; state xors 41.7% over the interim animation floor 0.4%. The design carries its own 1-px outline, so the outline pass is off.
